title: Halo-Halo
subtitle: filipino shaved ice dessert
excerpt: Halo-halo is a Filipino dessert of shaved ice layered with sweet toppings including coconut, mango, cooked sweet potato, and cashews, all finished with a drizzle of coconut milk. The name means mix-mix in Tagalog. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Halo-halo is the quintessential Filipino summer dessert. Toppings vary widely by region and preference; the key is the contrast between cold shaved ice, creamy coconut milk, and the various sweet components.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and chill the sweet potato up to 2 days ahead. The coconut cream can be made ahead and refrigerated. Assemble just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Filipino dessert of shaved ice topped with sweet ingredients and coconut milk. The name means mix-mix in Tagalog, referring to the instruction to stir everything together before eating.
Purple yam widely used in Filipino desserts. It has a mildly sweet, nutty flavour and a vivid purple colour. Sweet potato can be used as a substitute.

The instruction in the name is the instruction for eating it. Mix everything together before you start. The ice melts into the coconut milk and the toppings combine into something greater than their parts.

content.text: Cook the sweet potato cubes in a small saucepan with the sugar and just enough water to cover. Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until tender and the liquid is syrupy. Cool, then refrigerate until chilled.
Stir the sugar into the chilled coconut milk until dissolved. Set aside.
Prepare the optional rice crisps. Spread cooked rice thinly on a baking tray and let it dry for an hour or overnight. Pan-fry in a little oil over high heat until puffed and golden. Drain and cool.
To assemble, fill each tall glass or bowl one third full with crushed ice or shaved ice. Add the sweet potato, mango, and cashews over the ice.
Pour 3 to 4 tablespoons of the sweetened coconut milk over each serving. Top with rice crisps if using.
Serve immediately with a long spoon. Mix everything together before eating.

attrs.problem: The ice is melting too quickly.
attrs.solution: Chill the glasses in the freezer for 10 minutes before assembling. Work fast once you start building.

attrs.problem: The sweet potato is too firm.
attrs.solution: Cook it for a few more minutes until a fork goes through easily. The cubes should be tender all the way through.
Reduce the sugar in both the sweet potato and the coconut milk. Very ripe mango also adds significant sweetness, so adjust before serving.

content.text: Halo-halo is the defining Filipino dessert. It is sold at snack bars, restaurants, and street stalls across the country. The toppings vary by vendor and by what is in season. Classic versions include red beans, coconut jelly, plantain in syrup, and ube ice cream on top. This simplified version captures the spirit of the dish with ingredients that are easy to find.
